title: The Scary Truth About Third Party Auto Warranties
summary: A consumer-law channel relays a former claims rep's account of dealer markup, backdated paperwork scams, exclusions and payout caps on third-party auto warranties.

assertions.quote: the dealers can then sell them for whatever the finance guy feels he can get by with often five to ten times the cost
you file it now and say you sold them the car today or you sold it to them yesterday

verdicts.note: Documented in specific lawsuits and whistleblower accounts, but there's no base-rate data showing this is common rather than an isolated bad-actor practice.

assertions.quote: they might exclude a known problem like i don't know a dual clutch transmission in a ford product

verdicts.note: Vehicle-specific exclusions for known problem components are a commonly reported feature of aftermarket vehicle service contracts.

assertions.quote: engine failures are often a customer's fault such as running low on oil neglected maintenance etc

verdicts.note: Maintenance-related exclusions are standard contract language, and inspectors routinely cite lack of maintenance to deny expensive claims.

assertions.quote: this contract does not have to pay out more than two thousand dollars

verdicts.note: Payout caps exist in some lower-cost contracts, though they are not universal across all providers.

assertions.quote: on average they have to pay substantially less than four hundred dollars per warranty over the entire pool of every warranty
what matters is what's written on the contract and an extended service contract is in fact a contract

verdicts.note: Written contract terms generally govern over verbal sales statements in consumer contract law, barring rare fraud exceptions.

assertions.quote: you got to read the fine print read all the stuff

verdicts.note: Exclusions, caps and service restrictions are disclosed in the contract text, so reading it surfaces limits a sales pitch would omit.
